land.text: Seville and its district: the page gives no boundary, only that Abu al-Qasim 'declared independence from the Caliphate of Cordoba'

predecessors.note: The page dates the birth 1023 (lead and infobox) but its body says independence came 'after its downfall in 1031'; Cliopatria starts the shape in 1028.

land.text: all that Seville still held when al-Mu'tamid surrendered it in September 1091

successors.note: Algeciras had passed to the Almoravids in July 1086 and Córdoba in early 1091.

capitals.name: Seville (Ishbīliya)
capitals.note: Infobox 'Capital: Seville'. The al-Mu'tamid page calls Córdoba 'the capital' when it was taken in 1070, but the court stayed at Seville; no second capital is recorded.

rulers.name: Abu al-Qasim Muhammad ibn Abbad (Abbad I)
rulers.note: 'The first emir of Seville was Abu al-Qasim (1023–1042).'

rulers.name: Abbad II al-Mu'tadid
rulers.note: Died 28 February 1069; the Seville page gives 1042–1069.

rulers.name: Muhammad al-Mu'tamid ibn Abbad
rulers.note: Taken captive and exiled to Aghmat in 1091 (September, per the Almoravid page).

correction.text: the 1028 core shape applied back to 1023; the page names only the city and its taifa

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the page dates the taifa to 1023 ('was established in 1023'; first emir Abu al-Qasim 1023–1042) but Cliopatria's first shape starts in 1028. The extent in 1023-1027 is not on any page opened, so the 1028 core shape is applied back to 1023 (confidence 1 on the extent).

11,517 km2: Seville and its district, the core. The infobox gives no area, so only the shape's size and bbox were checked. Gains made inside this span (Mértola 1044-45, Huelva and Santa Maria do Algarve 1051, Niebla 1053, Algeciras 1055) are in the ledger and are what the 1056 shape shows.

correction.text: shape unchanged; it holds from 1055 (Algeciras) and the 1044-1054 gains are drawn from the ledger

keyframe_review.note: 26,113 km2, west to the Algarve and south to Algeciras: the sum of Huelva (1051), Santa Maria do Algarve (1051), Niebla (1053) and Algeciras (1055), so the shape belongs from 1055, not 1056; apply the 1051-1054 gains from the ledger. 'Algeciras (1055)', 'Huelva (1051)', 'Mértola (1044–45)'.

35,187 km2: the shape now reaches the Atlantic coast of the Algarve (Silves, taken 1063 per the Silves infobox) and holds Ronda (1065), Carmona and Morón (both 1066). Silves and Ronda enter two to three years before the shape begins; the ledger dates them.

correction.text: shape unchanged; it holds 1070-1074 and 1078-1084 (Córdoba lost 1075, regained 1078)

keyframe_review.note: 62,252 km2: Córdoba (1070, 'The capital, Córdoba was taken in 1070, lost in 1075, and regained in 1078') and Arcos (1069) are inside, so the shape begins in 1070, not 1072, and omits Córdoba in 1075-1077 (new keyframe 1075). The Toledo page dates the loss of the Cordoban lands to 1077.

correction.text: the 1072 shape without Córdoba, lost in 1075 and regained in 1078

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for the three years Córdoba was out of Seville's hands: taken by Toledo with Alfonso VI's help in 1075 (Toledo page), regained in 1078 (al-Mu'tamid page).

correction.text: the 1085 shape without Algeciras and its district, ceded to the Almoravids in July 1086; it holds 1078-1091

keyframe_review.note: 92,473 km2, east to Murcia (taken 1078) and including Córdoba again: the shape is right from 1078, not 1085, but it ends in 1091, not 1093 (Seville surrendered 'In September 1091'), and Algeciras left in July 1086 when al-Mu'tamid agreed to give it to Ibn Tashfin as a base. The first version subtracted Cliopatria's 'Taifa of Algeciras' 1085 shape; that shape is in Málaga province, does not meet this one (intersection empty) and left Algeciras drawn as Seville's until 1091, so the district is now subtracted by name (4 grid cells, about 1,000 km2). The shape grows by about 30,000 km2 over the 1072 shape; Murcia's Cliopatria shape (6,298 km2, 1078) explains a part. By overlay the 1085 shape also holds Jaén province and the Lorca country (54 grid cells, about 13,700 km2, against 3 cells in the 1072 shape) and part of Málaga province (10 cells). No page opened gives them to Seville: the Jaén page has 'Jaén was conquered by Habbus al-Muzaffar, leader of the Zirid Taifa of Granada' (undated) and 'conquered by the Almoravids in 1091', without Seville; the Lorca page has an independent taifa 'first created in 1042'; the Ibn Ammar page has no campaign; the Taifa of Seville page names none of these places (all read 2026-10-25). Unverified and kept as drawn; the Granada dossier's 1085 loss to an 'unnamed neighbour' (taifa-of-granada ledger/8) may be the other side of it.

ledger.note: 1023: Abu al-Qasim founds the Abbadid taifa of Seville after the fall of the Caliphate of Córdoba. 'The first emir of Seville was Abu al-Qasim (1023–1042)'; the lead says it 'was established in 1023', though the body has him declare independence 'after its downfall in 1031'. The page gives the city, not a boundary.

region.text: Aznalcázar, Tocina and the Triana quarter, west and south of the city

ledger.note: 1036: Granada's coalition attacks Seville. 'They attacked Seville directly on or around 30 August 1036'; the allies from Almería and Écija occupied Aznalcázar and Tocina and burned the Triana quarter.

region.text: the countryside near Écija, east of Seville

ledger.note: 1039: the Zirids beat the Abbadids near Écija. 'In 1039, the Zirids also defeated the Abbadids of Seville in battle near Écija'; the page says Granada gained 'some territory to the west' but names no land, so no loss is drawn.

1044: Seville takes Mértola. The list of Abbad II's conquests reads 'Mértola (1044–45)'; the Mértola page (read again 2026-10-25): 'After the fall of the Caliphate of Córdoba, in 1031, Mértola became an independent taifa state, until it was conquered by the taifa of Seville in 1044-1045', so the land comes from the independent Taifa of Mértola (the Taifa article: 'Mértola: 1033–1044 (Tayfurid Dynasty); 1044–1091 (to Seville)'). The Mértola page does not name the ruler it was taken from; a dossier taifa-of-mertola is needed.

region.text: the taifa of Saltés and Huelva

ledger.note: 1051: Seville conquers Huelva and Saltés. Infobox 'Conquered by Seville: 1051'; 'From 1051 until 1091 it was under the forcible control of Seville'; Abbad II page: 'Huelva (1051)'.

region.cliopatria: Taifa of Santa Maria do Algarve
region.text: the Algarve coast around Santa Maria

ledger.note: 1051: Seville conquers Santa Maria do Algarve. Infobox 'Conquered by the Taifa of Seville: 1051'; 'From 1051 until 1091, it was under the forcible control of Seville'.
1053: Seville takes Niebla. 'From 1053 until 1091 it was under the forcible control of Taifa of Seville, by Abbad II al-Mu'tadid'; infobox 'To Seville/Almoravid dynasty: 1053–1091'.

1055: Seville takes Algeciras. 'Algeciras (1055)'; the Algeciras page: 'In 1055 al-Mu'tamid ibn Abbad, lord of Seville, appeared under Algeciras' walls, forcing Muhammad to leave the taifa' (the Taifa of Algeciras infobox and the Taifa list say 1058). Region revised after review: the first version drew Cliopatria's 1040 Algeciras shape, which is mostly Málaga province (15 of its 21 grid cells), land that Seville's own 1056 shape does not hold.

region.text: the westernmost Algarve around Silves and Cape St Vincent

ledger.note: 1063: Seville annexes Silves. 'the kingdom was conquered by the more powerful taifa of Seville' under Isa III, whose reign list ends 1063; infobox 'To Seville/Almoravid dynasty: 1063–1091'. The year comes from the infobox and emir list, not from the sentence.
1065: Seville conquers Ronda. 'Ronda (1065)'. The same page has Abbad II receiving the Berber princes of Ronda in 1053 and killing them in his steam bath.
1066: Seville conquers Carmona. 'first from 1013 to 1066 when it was conquered by the Taifa of Seville'; infobox 'To Seville/Almoravid dynasty: 1066–1091'.
1066: Seville conquers Morón. Infobox 'Conquered by the Taifa of Seville: 1066'; 'From 1066 until 1091 it was under the forcible control of Seville, ruled by Abbad II al-Mu'tadid'.
1069: Seville takes Arcos. 'Arcos (1069)', the last of Abbad II's conquests before his death on 28 February 1069. The Arcos page of the taifa gives 1068.

1070: al-Mu'tamid takes Córdoba. 'The capital, Córdoba was taken in 1070, lost in 1075, and regained in 1078'; the Toledo page: 'this ended with the city being captured by Seville in 1070' (Cliopatria dates its Seville shape with Córdoba from 1072). The region is the province, my reading of the city's taifa. The Taifa of Seville page itself reads 'Al-Mu'tamid seized Córdoba in 1071, with a brief interlude in 1075–1078' (page read again 2026-10-25; it does not mention 1070); 1070 is kept from the al-Mu'tamid and Toledo pages, 1071 is the Seville page's variant.

1075: Córdoba is lost to Toledo. Alfonso VI 'helped Al-Mamun of Toledo in conquering the taifa of Córdoba in 1075' (the al-Mu'tamid page: 'lost in 1075'). The Toledo page also says 'The Cordoban lands were lost in 1077'.
1078: al-Mu'tamid regains Córdoba ('regained in 1078'). The Toledo page does not date the return.

1078: Seville takes Murcia. 'From 1078 until 1091 it was under the forcible control of Seville, by Abbad II al-Mu'tadid' (sic; the al-Mu'tamid page has him declare himself 'Emir of Murcia' and later lose it with Ibn Ammar taken hostage, undated). Cliopatria keeps a Murcian shape to 1084.

1086 (July): al-Mu'tamid gives Algeciras to the Almoravids. 'As a condition for his assistance, Ibn Tashfin demanded that Algeciras be surrendered to him so he could use it as a base for his troops. Al-Mu'tamid agreed'; an advance force of 500 took it 'in July 1086 without encountering resistance'. Region revised after review: the first version drew Cliopatria's 1085 Algeciras shape, which lies in Málaga province (the Antequera and Coín country) and does not contain Algeciras.

region.text: Córdoba and the road to Seville

ledger.note: 1091: the Almoravids take Córdoba and turn on Seville. 'In early 1091, the Almoravids took control of Cordoba and turned towards Seville.'
1091: Córdoba falls to the Almoravids ('the Almoravids took control of Cordoba', early 1091; no month).

region.text: Córdoba and the road to Seville

ledger.note: 1091 (September): the contest ends with the surrender of Seville.

region.text: all that remained: Seville and the lands conquered since 1044

ledger.note: 1091 (September): al-Mu'tamid surrenders Seville and the Abbadid taifa ends. 'In September 1091, al-Mu'tamid surrendered Seville to the Almoravids and was exiled to Aghmat.' The Seville page ends it 'in 1091'; Cliopatria keeps the shape to 1093. Murcia, Niebla, Carmona and the rest pass to the Almoravids too (Murcia infobox 'To Seville/Almoravids: 1078–1091 / 1091–1145').

wars.name: Abbadid conquests of the south and west

zones.cliopatria: Taifa of Santa Maria do Algarve

wars.outcome: Seville annexes each neighbour in turn; Seville grows from about 11,500 to about 35,000 km2 by Cliopatria's shapes.
wars.note: Abbad II page: the conquests 'Mértola (1044–45)', 'Huelva (1051)', 'Algeciras (1055)', 'Ronda (1065)', 'Arcos (1069)'; the page names no individual battle.

wars.name: Granada–Seville wars

zones.text: near Écija and the lands west of it

wars.outcome: The Zirid coalition attacked Seville in 1036 and beat it near Écija in 1039, gaining unnamed land to the west; Seville beat the Zirids at Cabra in 1079. No lasting border move is named.
wars.note: Cabra 1079: 'The Zirids were defeated in the Battle of Cabra in 1079 against the forces of Seville.' Abbad II 'fought against the Zirids of Granada and the Aftasids of Badajoz, but with no conclusive results' (undated).

wars.name: Ferdinand I's campaign against Seville
wars.outcome: 'In 1063, when Ferdinand I appeared with an army on the outskirts of Seville', al-Mu'tadid accepted his suzerainty and paid tribute; the page gives no amount. No land changed hands.
wars.note: Seville was a tributary of León-Castile from 1063 (and of Alfonso VI later: 'Seville began paying tribute to King Alfonso VI of Castile', no year). The Castile and León dossiers should carry the vassal tint; the vassal event is theirs to record.

wars.name: Battle of Sagrajas
wars.outcome: On 23 October 1086 Alfonso VI 'was soundly defeated and forced to retreat north in disorder' by Yusuf ibn Tashfin, whom al-Mu'tamid supported. No border moved at once; it opened Iberia to the Almoravids.
wars.note: The Seville and al-Mu'tamid pages: 'Al-Mu'tamid supported the Almoravid ruler Yusuf ibn Tashfin against Alfonso in the Battle of Sagrajas in 1086.'

wars.name: Almoravid conquest of Seville
wars.outcome: Córdoba taken in early 1091; Seville surrendered in September 1091 and al-Mu'tamid was exiled to Aghmat; the Abbadid taifa ended.

certainty.note: No page opened gives a treaty line or survey: the pages name towns and taifas, not boundaries. The Atlantic and Mediterranean coasts and the Guadalquivir valley are the firm parts; the frontier with Badajoz and Toledo, and the Murcia exclave, are approximate.

notes: Dates are the pages'; where pages disagree the ledger note says so. (1) Start: the lead and infobox say 1023, the body 'after its downfall in 1031'; Cliopatria starts 1028. (2) End: the pages say 1091 (September, Almoravid page); Cliopatria keeps the shape to 1093. (3) Algeciras: 1055 on the Abbad II page and in the Algeciras body, 1058 in the Algeciras infobox and the Taifa list. (4) Arcos: 1069 on the Abbad II page, 1068 on the Arcos taifa page. (5) Córdoba: 1070 (Seville, al-Mu'tamid and Toledo pages), lost 1075 (al-Mu'tamid and Toledo pages) or 1077 (Toledo page's 'Cordoban lands'), regained 1078; the first Taifa of Córdoba (to 1070) has no dossier in the group: taifa-of-cordoba starts in 1147 and the caliphate dossier ends in 1031. (6) The +30,000 km2 of the Cliopatria 1085 shape over the 1072 shape is not explained by any dated page beyond Murcia 1078; a gap-filler should open the Murcia and Badajoz pages and the Almoravid conquest of Murcia. (7) Seville was tributary to León-Castile from 1063; the vassal event belongs in the Castile and León dossiers (no event type records being a vassal). (8) Morón, Arcos, Ronda, Niebla, Carmona, Silves, Murcia: counterparts with dossiers in the group. Mértola is named as conquered in 1044-45 on the Abbad II page and has no Cliopatria row: a dossier (taifa-of-mertola) is needed, its years unknown. (9) Names for the gazetteer: Mértola (place). (10) Infobox gives no area; shapes were judged by size and bbox only. (11) The first-period list in the Taifa article reads 'Seville: 1023–1091 (to Almoravids)'. (12) Review of 2026-10-25: the Algeciras regions of the 1055 gain, the July 1086 loss and the 1085 correction used Cliopatria's 'Taifa of Algeciras' shapes, which are Málaga-province land and not Algeciras; all three now name Algeciras with a 30 km radius, matching taifa-of-algeciras. (13) Mértola: independent taifa from 1031 (Mértola page), conquered 1044-45; the counterpart taifa-of-mertola still needs a dossier. (14) Jaén, Baeza and Lorca are inside the 1085 shape and in none of the earlier ones; no page opened gives them to Seville (Jaén was Granada's, Lorca an independent taifa from 1042); unverified, see the 1085 keyframe.
